aliases: Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation
summary: An elective imperial framework joining a changing collection of kingdoms, principalities, ecclesiastical territories and cities in central Europe.
military: Imperial estates contributed troops or money under negotiated obligations; imperial defense depended on cooperation among territorial rulers.
contributions: Imperial institutions provided a durable framework for political negotiation and legal order across fragmented central Europe.
origin: Otto I’s imperial coronation in Rome in 962 joined German royal power to renewed claims of Roman imperial authority.
decline: Napoleonic victories and political reorganization preceded Francis II’s abdication and dissolution of the empire in 1806.
periodNote: 962 follows the conventional chronology used by the German Historical Museum, beginning with Otto I’s imperial coronation. It describes this empire, rather than all earlier claims to Roman imperial succession.
